text: The EU has opened a formal antitrust investigation into Meta's policy limiting how AI providers can use WhatsApp's Business API. Meta's October policy restricts AI providers from delivering services to customers via WhatsApp when the AI is the primary product. EU concern: the policy may block third-party AI competitors from accessing a dominant communication platform (WhatsApp). Fines can reach 10% of global annual revenue. Trump has threatened counter-investigations and tariffs against the EU's actions targeting US tech firms.

meta.note: Regulatory architecture shift affecting AI distribution, competition, Meta's platform strategy, and geopolitical tech tensions.

text: U.S. employers have announced 1.17 million layoffs YTD — the highest since 2020. November layoffs: 71,321 (down from October's massive 153k, but still historically elevated). Drivers include: restructuring (top cited), AI-driven displacement (54,694 layoffs this year attributed to AI), tariffs, market/economic conditions, and closings. Hiring plans remain depressed: 497,151 announced hires YTD, down 35% from 2024. Meanwhile, weekly jobless claims unexpectedly fell to 191k, lowest in 3+ years — a direct statistical inversion relative to layoff announcements.

meta.note: Long-arc labor fracture, AI displacement exposure, authority-split, and statistical inversion.

text: Paramount Skydance sends a formal letter to Warner Bros. Discovery accusing WBD of conducting a biased sale process favoring Netflix. The letter cites reports of predetermined outcomes, management conflicts of interest, possible EU regulatory signaling against a Paramount merger, and demands confirmation of an independent special committee to ensure a fair process.

meta.note: Major governance fracture exposing bias, misaligned incentives, and structural instability across the media infrastructure stack.

text: The Government Accountability Office (GAO) has opened an investigation into Federal Housing Authority Director Bill Pulte. Pulte has acted as an attack dog for President Donald Trump, targeting Trump's political enemies, this year. The investigation was opened at the request of a group of Senate Democrats.

meta.note: This is a major governance-layer signal, as it touches the federal housing regulator, Congressional oversight, DOJ referral behavior, and political weaponization of administrative authority — all core infrastructure.

text: The FBI arrested a suspect believed to have placed pipe bombs outside the Republican and Democratic party headquarters before the Jan. 6 Capitol riot. The suspect, Brian Cole Jr., of Woodbridge, Virginia, is charged with "use of an explosive device," U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi said. The investigation is ongoing and more charges could be filed, Bondi noted.

meta.note: This is not merely a criminal arrest; it is a federal legitimacy event.

text: Apple's general counsel, Kate Adams, and its vice president for environment, policy, and social initiatives, Lisa Jackson, are retiring from the company. The two executives reported to Apple CEO Tim Cook and are the latest members of senior leadership to exit the iPhone maker. In recent weeks, Apple's head software designer said he was leaving for Meta, while Apple is losing its AI head and chief operating officer to retirement.

meta.note: Apple shifts to legal defense as talent flows reverse and politics reshape leadership.
